title: Systems of Linear Equations
formula: \begin{cases} y = m_1x + b_1 \\ y = m_2x + b_2 \end{cases}
summary: A system is two equations at once. The solution is the point where the two lines cross.
explanation: Each equation is a line. The solution (x, y) has to work in BOTH equations.
On a graph, that means the point where the lines meet.
Same slope, different intercept = parallel lines = no solution. Same line twice = infinitely many solutions.
watchFor: Move the sliders until the lines cross somewhere new — the solution point follows.
Set both slopes equal. The lines never cross, so the solution point disappears.

steps: Both equal y, so set them equal: x + 2 = -x - 4.
